Title: fix(judge): a pitfall's feedback quotes the units where it is present
Head: d1c111016fd3818c9ec18891a03b11dd9adda34d on fix/judge-pitfall-notes; base: v1

A pitfall's feedback now quotes the reason from the units where the pitfall is present, not the units where it is absent.

## Why

The judge kept a unit's reason only on a "no" answer (`resolve.ts` dropped the reason on "yes", and `index.ts` recorded notes only when `met === false`). For a gate or a positive check a "no" is the defect, so that was right. For a pitfall the defect is a "yes", so a pitfall's feedback read like this, from sleeper waivers week 9 v2:

> pitfall pitfalls.bye_coverage (1 of 3): claim1: Gesicki's own bye is Week 6 … so no bye inside the lead time is missed …; claim2: Juwan Johnson's bye is week 8 … he does not miss a bye

The reviser is told a pitfall is present and then given only reasons why it isn't. Across the 44 judged sleeper cards on prod, `bye_coverage` and `crowd_metric_as_value` fire on 6 of 7 and 5 of 7 waivers cards, and none of those verdicts says where the pitfall was.

## Change

Title: fix(sleeper): waivers checks stop faulting ownership read as scarcity
Head: 52574e7c92af185dbdde771019f93813b340f0d8 on fix/sleeper-waivers-crowd-checks; base: v1

Two waivers checks stop faulting a claim for how it treats ownership. `ranked_on_usage` asks only about role and usage, or for a team defense or kicker, its matchup. `crowd_metric_as_value` fires only when a crowd number is offered as evidence the player will score.

## Why

On prod, `ranked_on_usage` failed 5 of 7 judged waivers cards. Its question also required "trending and ownership counts framed as scarcity", so the judge failed claims that never mention them: "grounds the rank purely in role … but the 59.7% ownership figure is not framed as scarcity". `crowd_metric_as_value` already guards a crowd number used as value.

With #2198 the pitfall's reasons became visible, and they showed it firing on ownership used as how hard a player is to land: "cites the 49.2% ownership number … 'leaves ~5 teams without him, safer to land at priority 8'". That framing is the one the rubric wants.

## Checked

github.review.content:
## Takeaway
Moving `bye_coverage` from a per-claim model question to code is the right call and is well tested; one window-boundary question (does the current week count as "inside the lead time"?) is worth confirming before it hardens.

## Verdict
comment

## Findings
- question: v1/packages/sleeper/src/waivers/rubric.ts:66 — the unflagged window is `r.bye >= f.week && r.bye <= f.week + BYE_LEAD`, which includes the current week, while the prompt step 6 and the pre-existing rule say "inside the **next** two weeks". The hole half has the mirror image: `facts.ts:82` computes holes over `[week, week+1, week+2]`, so a claim is counted as covering a hole in the current week even though a waiver picked up this week presumably cannot play this week. If current-week byes are in scope, the prompt should say so; if they are not, both halves are one week wide in the direction that penalizes the writer. I could not settle Sleeper's pickup-availability timing from the repo, so I am asking rather than calling it a defect.
- nit: v1/packages/sleeper/test/waivers.test.ts:262 — the faux judge's "answer no" regex still alternates on `miss a bye inside the lead time`, a question that no longer exists in the rubric. It is dead text now that the check is code; dropping the alternative keeps the helper honest.
- nit: v1/packages/sleeper/src/waivers/rubric.ts:64 — the keyword match misses a few flagged-by shapes: "byes" (plural, no `\bbye\b` match in it) and "sits wk. 10" (the sentence gap refuses a `.` before whitespace, so "wk." breaks the match). Both miss in the lenient direction and the prompt prescribes the "sits wk 10" form, so this is acceptable; just be aware a writer who uses either form still gets penalized.

## Verified
- Read the full diff against `origin/v1` plus the surrounding code: `facts.ts`, `rubric.ts`, `card.ts`, and the judge (`v1/packages/judge/src/index.ts`, `rubric.ts`). Pitfall scoring applies `penalty = -weight * met` where `met` is the share of units the pitfall is present in; the new `met = flaws.length / (holes.length + rows.length)` with at most one flaw per hole and per row is in exactly that range and the same semantics as the old row-scoped question. `codeResults` records `detail` as the note, so the reviser is told the named flaw, in line with #2198.
- No remaining references to `bye_exposure` anywhere; `Bye` is constructed only in `teamNeeds` (`facts.ts:86`), so adding `short` to the type breaks no other producer or consumer.
- Ran `node --test packages/sleeper/test/*.test.ts` after a clean checkout: 141/141 pass, matching the PR's claim, including the new `bye_coverage` test (clean card, open hole, unflagged add, flagged phrasings, another team's week, decimals, pre-`short` facts) and the `sleeper.waivers@6` assertions in both workflow tests.
- Ran `node --test tools/bundle-locks.test.ts`: the version-3 bump in `agent.json` matches the recomputed `version.lock` hash.
- Exercised the `flags` regex directly in node: "sits wk 10." (trailing period) and "on bye in week 10" flag; "proj 4.11" does not name week 11, "proj 4.10" does not name week 10; another team's "week 11 bye" does not flag a week-10 add; the match stays inside one sentence ("Sits wk 10. Bears bye is wk 11." is fine; a `;`-separated second sentence does not leak in).
- The check follows the existing whole-card code-pitfall pattern (`faab_language_on_rolling`), reads the same `facts` unit the model checks get, and dropping the row question removes one model call per claim, as the description says.
- CI: `check=success`, `image=skipped`; no Go changes in the diff.

## Notes
- The `h.short ?? 1` fallback is exact for the recorded pre-`short` cards only because every hole there has `out: 1`; a shared bye in old recorded facts would undercount as one slot. Fine while those recordings are the only consumers, worth remembering when replaying older sessions.
- One flaw now costs a smaller `met` share on a card with many rows than a per-claim "yes" did, since the denominator is holes + rows — that is the same share-of-units convention the rubric already uses, and the weight (−2) is unchanged.
- The `?? 1` on a required `Bye.short` reads like defensive coding against a shape the type says cannot happen; the comment makes clear it is for recorded facts, which is reasonable given the eval adapter replays them.
